title: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics (Standard) · Practice paper 3
subject: Mathematics (Standard)
label: Practice paper
instr: This question paper contains 38 questions. All questions are compulsory.
This question paper is divided into five sections: A, B, C, D and E.
In Section A, questions 1 to 18 are multiple choice questions (MCQs) and questions 19 and 20 are assertion-reason based questions of 1 mark each.
In Section B, questions 21 to 25 are very short answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each.
In Section C, questions 26 to 31 are short answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each.
In Section D, questions 32 to 35 are long answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each.
In Section E, questions 36 to 38 are case study based questions carrying 4 marks each. Each has three sub-parts (i), (ii) and (iii) of 1, 1 and 2 marks respectively.

There is no overall choice. However, an internal choice has been provided in 2 questions in Section B, 2 questions in Section C and 2 questions in Section D. An internal choice has been provided in all the sub-parts having 2 marks of the questions in Section E.
Draw neat and clean figures wherever required. Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ wherever required, if not stated.
Use of calculators is not allowed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The product of a non-zero rational number and an irrational number is:
questions.sol: If $r \neq 0$ is rational and $r \times x = q$ were rational for an irrational $x$, then $x = \frac{q}{r}$ would be rational, which is not true. So the product is always irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $-2$ is a zero of the polynomial $x^2 + kx - 6$, then its other zero is:
questions.sol: $p(-2) = 4 - 2k - 6 = 0 \Rightarrow k = -1$. The polynomial is $x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2)$, so the other zero is 3. (Also, product of zeroes $= -6$, so the other zero $= \frac{-6}{-2} = 3$.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The pair of equations $x = 4$ and $y = -3$ represents, graphically, two lines which are:
questions.sol: $x = 4$ is a line parallel to the y-axis and $y = -3$ is a line parallel to the x-axis. They meet at the point $(4, -3)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The quadratic equation $kx^2 - 6x + 1 = 0$ has two distinct real roots if:
questions.sol: For a quadratic equation, $k \neq 0$. Two distinct real roots need $D = 36 - 4k \gt 0$, i.e. $k \lt 9$. So $k \lt 9$ and $k \neq 0$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$. If AB = 4 cm, DE = 6 cm, EF = 9 cm and FD = 12 cm, then the perimeter of $\triangle ABC$ is:
questions.sol: Perimeter of $\triangle DEF = 6 + 9 + 12 = 27$ cm. For similar triangles, the ratio of perimeters equals the ratio of corresponding sides: $\frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$. Perimeter of $\triangle ABC = \frac{2}{3} \times 27 = 18$ cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The distance between the points $(a\cos\theta, 0)$ and $(0, a\sin\theta)$, where $a \gt 0$, is:
questions.sol: Distance $= \sqrt{a^2\cos^2\theta + a^2\sin^2\theta} = \sqrt{a^2(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta)} = \sqrt{a^2} = a$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\sin\theta = \cos\theta$, where $0^\circ \lt \theta \lt 90^\circ$, then the value of $2\tan\theta + \cos^2\theta$ is:
questions.sol: $\sin\theta = \cos\theta \Rightarrow \tan\theta = 1 \Rightarrow \theta = 45^\circ$. Value $= 2 \times 1 + \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = 2 + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: $(1 + \tan^2 A)(1 - \sin A)(1 + \sin A)$ is equal to:
questions.sol: $(1 + \tan^2 A) = \sec^2 A$ and $(1 - \sin A)(1 + \sin A) = 1 - \sin^2 A = \cos^2 A$. Product $= \sec^2 A \times \cos^2 A = 1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: TP and TQ are tangents drawn from an external point T to a circle with centre O and radius 5 cm. If TP and TQ are perpendicular to each other, then the length of each tangent is:
questions.sol: $\angle OPT = \angle OQT = 90^\circ$ and $\angle PTQ = 90^\circ$, so $\angle POQ = 90^\circ$ and OPTQ is a rectangle with OP = OQ. Hence it is a square, and TP = OP = 5 cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The circumference of a circle is equal to the perimeter of a square of side 11 cm. The area of the circle is:
questions.sol: $2\pi r = 4 \times 11 = 44 \Rightarrow r = 7$ cm. Area $= \frac{22}{7} \times 7 \times 7 = 154\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 6 cm is $6\pi\ \text{cm}^2$. The angle of the sector is:
questions.sol: $\frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi \times 6^2 = 6\pi \Rightarrow \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} = \frac{1}{6} \Rightarrow \theta = 60^\circ$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A right circular cylinder, a right circular cone and a hemisphere have the same base radius $r$, and the heights of the cylinder and the cone are also equal to $r$. The ratio of their volumes is:
questions.sol: Cylinder: $\pi r^3$; cone: $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^3$; hemisphere: $\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3$. Ratio $= 1 : \frac{1}{3} : \frac{2}{3} = 3 : 1 : 2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In the formula $\bar{x} = a + \frac{\sum f_i d_i}{\sum f_i}$ for finding the mean of grouped data, the $d_i$ are the deviations from the assumed mean $a$ of the:
questions.sol: In the assumed mean method, $d_i = x_i - a$, where $x_i$ are the class marks (mid-points) of the classes.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
For the following distribution, the sum of the lower limits of the median class and the modal class is:
Class0 - 1010 - 2020 - 3030 - 4040 - 50
Frequency5710126
questions.sol: N = 40, $\frac{N}{2} = 20$. Cumulative frequencies: 5, 12, 22, 34, 40, so the median class is 20 - 30 (lower limit 20). The highest frequency is 12, so the modal class is 30 - 40 (lower limit 30). Sum $= 20 + 30 = 50$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A letter is chosen at random from the letters of the word ASSOCIATION. The probability that the letter chosen is a vowel is:
questions.sol: ASSOCIATION has 11 letters, of which A, O, I, A, I, O, i.e. 6, are vowels. Probability $= \frac{6}{11}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers on them is 10 or more is:
questions.sol: Favourable outcomes: (4, 6), (5, 5), (6, 4), (5, 6), (6, 5), (6, 6), i.e. 6 out of 36. Probability $= \frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Tickets numbered 1 to 50 are mixed and one ticket is drawn at random. The probability that the number on it is a multiple of 3 or of 7 is:
questions.sol: Multiples of 3: 16; multiples of 7: 7; multiples of both (21 and 42): 2. Favourable $= 16 + 7 - 2 = 21$. Probability $= \frac{21}{50}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The point $(3, -4)$ is at a distance of 4 units from the x-axis and 5 units from the y-axis.
Reason (R): The distance of a point from the x-axis is the absolute value of its ordinate.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: Distance of $(3, -4)$ from the x-axis $= |-4| = 4$ units, but its distance from the y-axis $= |3| = 3$ units, not 5. So A is false. R is true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The graph of $y = x^2 - 6x + 9$ meets the x-axis at exactly one point.
Reason (R): $x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2$, which becomes zero only when $x = 3$.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: The graph meets the x-axis where $y = 0$, i.e. at the zeroes of the polynomial. R shows that the only zero is 3, so the graph meets the x-axis only at $(3, 0)$. Both are true and R explains A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Check whether $12^n$ can end with the digit 0 for any natural number $n$. Give a reason for your answer.
questions.model:
$12^n = (2^2 \times 3)^n = 2^{2n} \times 3^n$
A number ends with the digit 0 only if it is divisible by 10, i.e. by both 2 and 5, so 5 must appear in its prime factorisation.
The prime factors of $12^n$ are only 2 and 3. By the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic this factorisation is unique, so 5 is not a factor of $12^n$.
Hence $12^n$ cannot end with the digit 0 for any natural number $n$.

points.t: Reason: 5 is not a prime factor (uniqueness of factorisation), so $12^n$ cannot end with 0

or.text: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 2520. If one of the numbers is 72, find the other number and write it as a product of its prime factors.
or.model:
HCF $\times$ LCM = product of the two numbers
Other number $= \frac{12 \times 2520}{72} = \frac{30240}{72} = 420$
$420 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7$

points.t: Using HCF $\times$ LCM = product to get the other number = 420

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The sides of $\triangle ABC$ are AB = 4 cm, BC = 6 cm and CA = 8 cm, and the sides of $\triangle PQR$ are PQ = 9 cm, QR = 12 cm and RP = 6 cm. Check whether the two triangles are similar. If they are, write the similarity correspondence.
questions.model:
Arranging the sides in increasing order: $\triangle ABC$: AB = 4, BC = 6, CA = 8; $\triangle PQR$: RP = 6, PQ = 9, QR = 12.
$\frac{AB}{RP} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{BC}{PQ} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{CA}{QR} = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}$
All three ratios are equal, so the triangles are similar (SSS similarity criterion).
B is common to AB and BC, and P is common to RP and PQ, so B corresponds to P; similarly A corresponds to R and C to Q.
$\triangle ABC \sim \triangle RPQ$

points.t: Matching the sides in order and showing all three ratios equal $\frac{2}{3}$, so the triangles are similar (SSS)

or.text: In $\triangle ABC$, AD and BE are altitudes, with D on BC and E on AC. Prove that $CD \times CB = CE \times CA$.
or.model:
In $\triangle ADC$ and $\triangle BEC$:
$\angle ADC = \angle BEC = 90^\circ$ (AD and BE are altitudes)
$\angle ACD = \angle BCE$ (common angle C)
So $\triangle ADC \sim \triangle BEC$ (AA similarity criterion).
Hence $\frac{CD}{CE} = \frac{CA}{CB} \Rightarrow CD \times CB = CE \times CA$.

points.t: $\triangle ADC \sim \triangle BEC$ by AA (right angles and common angle C)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A chord of a circle of radius 10.5 cm subtends an angle of $120^\circ$ at the centre. Find the areas of the minor sector and the major sector formed by the two radii through the ends of the chord.
questions.model:
Area of the circle $= \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 = 346.5\ \text{cm}^2$
Area of minor sector $= \frac{120}{360} \times 346.5 = 115.5\ \text{cm}^2$
Area of major sector $= 346.5 - 115.5 = 231\ \text{cm}^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In a class of 40 students, 25 play cricket, 20 play football and 10 play both games. A student of the class is chosen at random. Find the probability that the student plays (i) neither of the two games, (ii) exactly one of the two games.
questions.model:
Students who play only cricket $= 25 - 10 = 15$; only football $= 20 - 10 = 10$; both $= 10$.
Students who play at least one game $= 15 + 10 + 10 = 35$, so neither $= 40 - 35 = 5$.
(i) P(neither) $= \frac{5}{40} = \frac{1}{8}$
(ii) Exactly one game: $15 + 10 = 25$ students. P(exactly one) $= \frac{25}{40} = \frac{5}{8}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the largest number which divides 245 and 1029 leaving a remainder 5 in each case.
questions.model:
The required number divides $245 - 5 = 240$ and $1029 - 5 = 1024$ exactly.
$240 = 2^4 \times 3 \times 5$
$1024 = 2^{10}$
HCF(240, 1024) $= 2^4 = 16$
The largest such number is 16. (Check: $245 = 16 \times 15 + 5$ and $1029 = 16 \times 64 + 5$.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the zeroes of the polynomial $3x^2 - 4x - 4$, find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are $\alpha^2$ and $\beta^2$.
questions.model:
$\alpha + \beta = \frac{4}{3}$ and $\alpha\beta = -\frac{4}{3}$
Sum of the new zeroes: $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = \frac{16}{9} + \frac{8}{3} = \frac{40}{9}$
Product of the new zeroes: $\alpha^2\beta^2 = (\alpha\beta)^2 = \frac{16}{9}$
Required polynomial $= k\left(x^2 - \frac{40}{9}x + \frac{16}{9}\right)$; taking $k = 9$: $9x^2 - 40x + 16$.
(Check: the zeroes of $3x^2 - 4x - 4$ are 2 and $-\frac{2}{3}$; their squares 4 and $\frac{4}{9}$ are the zeroes of $9x^2 - 40x + 16$.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The 5th term of an A.P. is 19, and its 12th term exceeds twice its 6th term by 1. Find the A.P. and the sum of its first 15 terms.
questions.model:
Let the first term be $a$ and the common difference be $d$.
$a + 4d = 19$ ...(1)
$a + 11d = 2(a + 5d) + 1 \Rightarrow a + 11d = 2a + 10d + 1 \Rightarrow d - a = 1$ ...(2)
From (2), $a = d - 1$. Substituting in (1): $5d - 1 = 19 \Rightarrow d = 4$, $a = 3$.
The A.P. is 3, 7, 11, 15, ...
$S_{15} = \frac{15}{2}[2 \times 3 + 14 \times 4] = \frac{15}{2} \times 62 = 465$

or.text: Find the sum of all three-digit natural numbers which leave a remainder 3 when divided by 7.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two concentric circles have centre O and radii 13 cm and 5 cm. AB is a chord of the larger circle which touches the smaller circle at P. Prove that P is the mid-point of AB, and find the length of AB.
questions.model:
AB touches the smaller circle at P, so AB is a tangent to the smaller circle and $OP \perp AB$ (radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact).
OP is also a perpendicular from the centre O to the chord AB of the larger circle. In right triangles OPA and OPB, OA = OB (radii of the larger circle) and OP is common, so $\triangle OPA \cong \triangle OPB$ (RHS) and AP = PB. Hence P is the mid-point of AB.
In right $\triangle OPA$: $AP = \sqrt{OA^2 - OP^2} = \sqrt{169 - 25} = \sqrt{144} = 12$ cm
AB $= 2 \times AP = 24$ cm

points.t: $OP \perp AB$ because AB is a tangent to the smaller circle at P
AP = PB (congruent right triangles OPA and OPB), so P is the mid-point

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In $\triangle PQR$, S is a point on the side QR such that $PS \perp QR$ and $PS^2 = QS \times SR$. Prove that $\angle QPR = 90^\circ$.
questions.model:
$PS^2 = QS \times SR \Rightarrow \frac{PS}{SR} = \frac{QS}{PS}$
In $\triangle PSQ$ and $\triangle RSP$: $\frac{QS}{PS} = \frac{PS}{SR}$ and $\angle PSQ = \angle RSP = 90^\circ$.
So $\triangle PSQ \sim \triangle RSP$ (SAS similarity criterion), and hence $\angle QPS = \angle PRS$.
In right $\triangle PSR$: $\angle PRS + \angle SPR = 90^\circ$.
$\angle QPR = \angle QPS + \angle SPR = \angle PRS + \angle SPR = 90^\circ$

points.t: Writing the ratio $\frac{QS}{PS} = \frac{PS}{SR}$ with the right angles at S
Using $\angle PRS + \angle SPR = 90^\circ$ to conclude $\angle QPR = 90^\circ$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Solve the following pair of linear equations graphically: $2x - y = 2$ and $x + y = 7$.
Also find the coordinates of the vertices of the triangle formed by these two lines and the x-axis, and find the area of this triangle.
questions.model:
For $2x - y = 2$, i.e. $y = 2x - 2$:
$x$013
$y$$-2$04
For $x + y = 7$, i.e. $y = 7 - x$:
$x$037
$y$740
Plot these points and draw the two lines on the same graph. The lines intersect at $(3, 4)$, so the solution is $x = 3$, $y = 4$.
The line $2x - y = 2$ meets the x-axis at $(1, 0)$ and the line $x + y = 7$ meets it at $(7, 0)$.
Vertices of the triangle: $(1, 0)$, $(7, 0)$ and $(3, 4)$.
Base (on the x-axis) $= 7 - 1 = 6$ units; height = 4 units (the y-coordinate of $(3, 4)$).
Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$ square units.

points.t: Correct table of at least two points for $2x - y = 2$
Correct table of at least two points for $x + y = 7$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
PA and PB are tangents drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm, touching it at A and B. OP = 10 cm, and OP intersects AB at M.
(i) Prove that OP is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
(ii) Find the length of the tangent PA.
(iii) Find the length of the chord AB.
questions.model:
(i) In $\triangle OAP$ and $\triangle OBP$: OA = OB (radii), $\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ$ (radius $\perp$ tangent) and OP is common. So $\triangle OAP \cong \triangle OBP$ (RHS), giving PA = PB and $\angle APO = \angle BPO$.
In $\triangle PAM$ and $\triangle PBM$: PA = PB, $\angle APM = \angle BPM$ and PM is common. So $\triangle PAM \cong \triangle PBM$ (SAS).
Hence AM = BM and $\angle AMP = \angle BMP$. As these angles form a linear pair, each is $90^\circ$. So OP is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
(ii) In right $\triangle OAP$: $PA = \sqrt{OP^2 - OA^2} = \sqrt{100 - 36} = 8$ cm.
(iii) AM is the altitude of right $\triangle OAP$ to its hypotenuse OP. Area of $\triangle OAP$: $\frac{1}{2} \times OA \times AP = \frac{1}{2} \times OP \times AM$
$\Rightarrow 6 \times 8 = 10 \times AM \Rightarrow AM = 4.8$ cm
AB $= 2 \times AM = 9.6$ cm.

points.t: $\triangle OAP \cong \triangle OBP$ (RHS), so $\angle APO = \angle BPO$ (with figure)
$\triangle PAM \cong \triangle PBM$ (SAS), so AM = BM and $\angle AMP = 90^\circ$
AM = 4.8 cm (using area of $\triangle OAP$ or similar triangles)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A solid model of a rocket is in the shape of a right circular cylinder of radius 3.5 cm and height 10 cm, with a right circular cone of the same radius and height 12 cm fixed on one end. Find the volume and the total surface area of the model.
questions.model:
$r = 3.5$ cm, height of cylinder $h = 10$ cm, height of cone $H = 12$ cm.
Slant height of cone $l = \sqrt{3.5^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{12.25 + 144} = \sqrt{156.25} = 12.5$ cm
Volume of cylinder $= \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 3.5 \times 10 = 385\ \text{cm}^3$
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 H = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 3.5 \times 12 = 154\ \text{cm}^3$
Volume of the model $= 385 + 154 = 539\ \text{cm}^3$
Curved surface area of cylinder $= 2\pi rh = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 10 = 220\ \text{cm}^2$; area of the free base $= \pi r^2 = 38.5\ \text{cm}^2$
Curved surface area of cone $= \pi rl = \frac{22}{7} \times 3.5 \times 12.5 = 137.5\ \text{cm}^2$
Total surface area $= 220 + 38.5 + 137.5 = 396\ \text{cm}^2$

points.t: CSA of cone $= 137.5\ \text{cm}^2$ and total surface area $= 396\ \text{cm}^2$

or.text: A solid toy is in the form of a hemisphere surmounted by a right circular cone of the same radius. The radius of the hemisphere is 10.5 cm and the height of the cone is 14 cm. Find the volume and the total surface area of the toy.
or.model:
$r = 10.5$ cm, $h = 14$ cm. Slant height $l = \sqrt{10.5^2 + 14^2} = \sqrt{110.25 + 196} = \sqrt{306.25} = 17.5$ cm
Volume of hemisphere $= \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 \times 10.5 = 2425.5\ \text{cm}^3$
Volume of cone $= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 \times 14 = 1617\ \text{cm}^3$
Volume of toy $= 2425.5 + 1617 = 4042.5\ \text{cm}^3$
CSA of hemisphere $= 2\pi r^2 = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 = 693\ \text{cm}^2$
CSA of cone $= \pi rl = \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 17.5 = 577.5\ \text{cm}^2$
Total surface area $= 693 + 577.5 = 1270.5\ \text{cm}^2$

points.t: CSA of cone $= 577.5\ \text{cm}^2$ and total surface area $= 1270.5\ \text{cm}^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A drone is hovering at a point vertically above a straight road. Two cars are on the road, one on each side of the drone, and are 400 m apart. The angles of depression of the two cars as seen from the drone are $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. Find the height of the drone above the road and the distance of each car from the point on the road directly below the drone.
questions.model:
Let D be the drone, F the point on the road directly below it, and DF $= h$ m. Let A and B be the cars, with the angles of depression of A and B equal to $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$. Then $\angle DAF = 60^\circ$ and $\angle DBF = 30^\circ$ (alternate angles), and AF + FB = 400 m.
In right $\triangle DFA$: $\tan 60^\circ = \frac{h}{AF} \Rightarrow AF = \frac{h}{\sqrt{3}}$
In right $\triangle DFB$: $\tan 30^\circ = \frac{h}{FB} \Rightarrow FB = \sqrt{3}h$
$\frac{h}{\sqrt{3}} + \sqrt{3}h = 400 \Rightarrow \frac{4h}{\sqrt{3}} = 400 \Rightarrow h = 100\sqrt{3}$ m
AF $= \frac{100\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = 100$ m and FB $= \sqrt{3} \times 100\sqrt{3} = 300$ m
The drone is $100\sqrt{3}$ m (about 173.2 m) high; the cars are 100 m and 300 m from the point below it.

or.text: A balloon is rising vertically. At one instant, an observer standing on level ground sees the balloon at an angle of elevation of $30^\circ$. After the balloon has risen a further 200 m, the angle of elevation becomes $60^\circ$. Find the distance of the observer from the point on the ground directly below the balloon, and the height of the balloon at the first instant.
or.model:
Let O be the observer and F the point on the ground directly below the balloon, with OF $= x$ m. Let the first height of the balloon be $h$ m, so its second height is $(h + 200)$ m.
$\tan 30^\circ = \frac{h}{x} \Rightarrow h = \frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}$ ...(1)
$\tan 60^\circ = \frac{h + 200}{x} \Rightarrow h + 200 = \sqrt{3}x$ ...(2)
From (1) and (2): $\sqrt{3}x - \frac{x}{\sqrt{3}} = 200 \Rightarrow \frac{2x}{\sqrt{3}} = 200 \Rightarrow x = 100\sqrt{3}$ m
$h = \frac{100\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = 100$ m
The observer is $100\sqrt{3}$ m (about 173.2 m) from the point below the balloon, and the balloon was first at a height of 100 m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
During a sports day, a ball is thrown vertically upwards from ground level. Its height $h$ (in metres) above the ground $t$ seconds after it is thrown is given by $h = 25t - 5t^2$.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Find the height of the ball 2 seconds after it is thrown.
(ii) Using the discriminant, check whether the ball can reach a height of 35 m.
parts.model: $25t - 5t^2 = 35 \Rightarrow t^2 - 5t + 7 = 0$. $D = (-5)^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 7 = 25 - 28 = -3 \lt 0$, so there is no real value of $t$. The ball cannot reach a height of 35 m.

points.t: $t^2 - 5t + 7 = 0$ with $D = -3 \lt 0$, so the ball cannot reach 35 m

parts.q: (iii) At what times is the ball at a height of 20 m?
parts.model:
$25t - 5t^2 = 20 \Rightarrow t^2 - 5t + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow (t - 1)(t - 4) = 0 \Rightarrow t = 1$ or $t = 4$.
The ball is at a height of 20 m after 1 second (going up) and after 4 seconds (coming down).

or.q: (iii) Using the condition for equal roots, find the greatest height reached by the ball.
or.model:
Let the greatest height be $H$ m. The ball reaches $H$ at only one instant, so $25t - 5t^2 = H$, i.e. $5t^2 - 25t + H = 0$, has equal roots.
$D = 625 - 20H = 0 \Rightarrow H = 31.25$ m (reached at $t = \frac{25}{10} = 2.5$ s).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
On a map drawn with a coordinate grid, Ravi's house is at the point A$(-3, 2)$ and his school is at the point B$(5, 8)$. A straight road joins A and B. The main road of the town runs along the y-axis. One unit on the map represents 100 m on the ground.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Find the actual distance between Ravi's house and his school.
(ii) A bus stop is at the mid-point of AB. Find its coordinates.
(iii) The road AB crosses the main road (the y-axis) at a point P. Find the ratio in which P divides AB, and the coordinates of P.
parts.model:
Let P divide AB in the ratio $k : 1$. The x-coordinate of P is 0: $\frac{5k - 3}{k + 1} = 0 \Rightarrow k = \frac{3}{5}$, so the ratio is $3 : 5$.
y-coordinate of P $= \frac{3 \times 8 + 5 \times 2}{3 + 5} = \frac{34}{8} = \frac{17}{4}$
P $= \left(0, \frac{17}{4}\right)$

or.q: (iii) A tea stall T is on the road AB such that AT : TB = 3 : 1. Find the coordinates of T.
or.model:
By the section formula with $m : n = 3 : 1$:
$x = \frac{3 \times 5 + 1 \times (-3)}{3 + 1} = \frac{12}{4} = 3$, $y = \frac{3 \times 8 + 1 \times 2}{3 + 1} = \frac{26}{4} = \frac{13}{2}$
T $= \left(3, \frac{13}{2}\right)$

points.t: Correct use of the section formula with ratio $3 : 1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
A school surveyed 50 students about the time (in minutes) they take to travel from home to school. The data are given below:
Time (in minutes)0 - 1010 - 2020 - 3030 - 4040 - 50
Number of students61015127
Based on the above information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Identify the modal class of the travel times.
parts.model: The highest frequency is 15, so the modal class is 20 - 30.

parts.q: (ii) How many students take less than 30 minutes to reach school?
(iii) Find the median time taken by the students.
parts.model:
$\frac{N}{2} = 25$. Cumulative frequencies: 6, 16, 31, 43, 50. The median class is 20 - 30.
$l = 20$, $cf = 16$, $f = 15$, $h = 10$
Median $= l + \frac{\frac{N}{2} - cf}{f} \times h = 20 + \frac{25 - 16}{15} \times 10 = 20 + 6 = 26$ minutes

or.q: (iii) Find the mode of the data.
